anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: The optimizer selects markedly sub-optimal execution plans even though statistics are accurate.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly: Sessions serialize on hot buffer pages and latches, causing CPU spin and wait amplification.
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly: The write-ahead logging path (log buffer, flush, and archiving) becomes the primary bottleneck on the commit path.

Combined phenomena: When these three root causes manifest together, the database shows erratic plan flips that drive excessive logical I/O, intense BUFFER_BUSY and LATCH_* waits, and rising LOG_FLUSH / LOG_SYNC latencies. Full scans or poorly chosen nested-loop joins repeatedly access the same root or leaf pages, heating them in the buffer pool and inflating latch contention. As transactions wait on both latches and commits, CPU utilization rises without matching throughput, checkpoints become more frequent, log files grow rapidly, and application response time oscillates unpredictably.

Causal chain: Sub-optimal plans increase page touch frequency and concentrate I/O on a narrow set of blocks, which escalates buffer-cache and latch contention. Prolonged latch waits lengthen transaction lifetimes, causing more redo to be generated and retained in memory. The swollen redo stream overtaxes the log subsystem; delayed log flushes extend commit latency, holding transactions and their latches even longer and further heating hot pages. Log stalls can also trigger additional optimizer recompilations and plan cache invalidations, risking another round of poor plan selection. The three anomalies therefore reinforce one another in a feedback loop that degrades both read and write paths and can quickly exhaust the system’s performance headroom.

entry.official_description: stacked diagnostics accessed without active handler
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
